answer: A delta of reputation can slow Sybil creation the way a river delta slows a flood: new identities start with almost no flow of trust, and earning capacity requires a long, verifiable history of useful work attested by distinct peers. A lone sparrow of an account cannot fake that watershed, because each attestation costs time, stake, or completed tasks, and duplicates sharing the same behaviour, timing, or funding trail are clustered and throttled. Attackers must therefore pay real cost per identity instead of minting thousands free.
